summary: Suggests defining a single access protocol, using one reserved socket, as the front door to the network's standard services. Commands such as USER, PASS, ACCT, MAIL, FTP and HELP would select the service wanted, and the proposed mail protocol could be the first to use it.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 552 suggests a single access protocol for reaching several network services. A user could connect through one reserved socket and choose a service with a command.

questions: what is the single access protocol proposal
subtitle: A proposal for one access protocol that could direct users to several network services.

tldr.problem: The author asks whether standard network protocols could be reached through a single access protocol before the proposed mail protocol became official.
tldr.mechanism: The suggested protocol would use a reserved socket and commands such as USER, PASS, ACCT, MAIL, FTP, RJS and BYE, with nested command and reply spaces.
tldr.outcome: The note proposes that the mail protocol could be the first protocol implemented under the shared access scheme. It does not settle what is free or how the protocols relate.

facts.label: Suggested services
facts.value: MAIL, FTP, RJS, and possibly DRS

today: The unit records RFC 552's status as Unknown and lists no updates or obsoleting RFCs. This document is a brief proposal for a single access protocol.

sections.title: One Access Point for Protocols
sections.content:
Buz Owen asks whether a single access protocol could be specified and assigned a reserved socket before the proposed mail protocol became official. Under this plan, the mail protocol might be the first to use the access protocol.

Other protocols could later be moved to it when implementors found convenient and after problems in the official specifications were addressed.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal is to make one network entry point available before the mail protocol is finalized. Other services could use it later as their specifications and implementations permit.

sections.title: Suggested Commands
sections.content:
The suggested command set includes USER, PASS and ACCT; service commands MAIL, FTP, RJS and possibly DRS; and possibly HELP, followed by BYE. The author says the design would follow Jim White's idea of nested command and reply spaces.

The question marks after DRS and HELP show that these were tentative entries in the list, not a finalized command set.
sections.plainLanguage: The list combines identity commands, commands for choosing services, and a command to leave. The author marks some possible commands as uncertain.

sections.title: Questions Left Open
sections.content:
The author explicitly says the single-access proposal does not answer what “free” means. It also leaves open how the different protocols relate to one another.

Owen says the proposal would not make those problems worse, though it would make them somewhat different. The RFC is a short question and proposal, not a complete specification.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal leaves important design questions unanswered, including what free service means and how protocols fit together. It offers a starting idea rather than a complete protocol.
